comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value option election for short-term structured liabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation elects to account for certain short-term borrowings, primarily short-term structured liabilities, under the fair value option because this debt is risk-managed on a fair value basis.
comparisons.comparison: While Citi details specific liquidity agreements and APAs for its conduits, Bank of America discusses the accounting treatment for certain short-term borrowings, primarily short-term structured liabilities, under the fair value option. Citi's disclosure is operational regarding the mechanics of liquidity support (APAs and lending commitments) for conduits, whereas Bank of America's disclosure is financial reporting oriented, focusing on why the fair value option is elected for specific debt instruments due to risk management practices. Both deal with short-term funding instruments, but Citi's focus is on the liquidity facility structure for conduits, while Bank of America's focus is on the valuation method for structured liabilities.

peer_results.rationale: Goldman Sachs candidates focus on accounting for hybrid financial instruments and unsecured short-term borrowings under the fair value option, and general secured financing refinancing risk management. These do not specifically address the mechanics of liquidity agreements, asset purchase agreements, or credit enhancement facilities for administered commercial paper conduits, which is the specific topic of Citi's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: To ensure timely repayment of commercial paper, each asset pool is associated with a minimum 100% deal-specific liquidity facility provided by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., which also supplies uncommitted program-wide liquidity and credit enhancement in the form of standby letters of credit approximating 10% of outstanding commercial paper.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan provide multi-seller commercial paper conduits with liquidity support consisting of deal-specific facilities and program-wide backstops. Citi describes these as transaction-specific asset purchase agreements (APAs) to purchase receivables at par, and short-term lending commitments for market disruptions. JPMorgan similarly provides a minimum 100% deal-specific liquidity facility and uncommitted program-wide liquidity/credit enhancement. A key similarity is that both firms provide these facilities to support commercial paper issuance for clients. However, Citi explicitly notes that funding under its APA may subject clients to increased interest costs, whereas JPMorgan's disclosure focuses on the existence of the facilities to ensure timely repayment without quantifying the cost impact on clients in this specific section.

sentences.text: Citigroup also provides the conduits with two forms of liquidity agreements that are used to provide funding to the conduits in the event of a market disruption, among other events.
Each asset of the conduits is supported by a transaction-specific liquidity facility in the form of an asset purchase agreement (APA).
Any funding under the APA will likely subject the underlying conduit clients to increased interest costs.

In addition, the Company provides the conduits with program-wide liquidity in the form of short-term lending commitments, where the Company has agreed to lend to the conduits in the event of a short-term disruption in the commercial paper market, subject to specified conditions.

To ensure timely repayment of the commercial paper, and to provide the conduits with funding to provide financing to customers in the event that the conduits do not obtain funding in the commercial paper market, each asset pool financed by the conduits has a minimum 100% deal-specific liquidity facility associated with it provided by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. also provides the multi-seller conduit vehicles with uncommitted program-wide liquidity facilities and program-wide credit enhancement in the form of standby letters of credit.

comparisons.peer_topic: Liquidity facilities for Municipal Tender Option Bonds
comparisons.peer_summary: Short-term securities are supported by a liquidity facility allowing investors to put their interests; while typically provided by a third-party, the Firm may provide this facility in some programs, and these facilities are classified as derivatives.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley provide liquidity facilities to support short-term securities issued by conduits or trusts. Citi provides liquidity agreements to its Citi-Administered Asset-Backed Commercial Paper Conduits to fund them in the event of market disruption. Similarly, Morgan Stanley supports short-term securities (specifically Municipal Tender Option Bonds) with liquidity facilities that allow investors to put their interests, provided by either a third party or the Firm. Both disclosures confirm the bank's role in providing this liquidity backstop to maintain the liquidity of the short-term instruments.

sentences.text: Citigroup also provides the conduits with two forms of liquidity agreements that are used to provide funding to the conduits in the event of a market disruption, among other events.
The short-term securities are supported by a liquidity facility pursuant to which the investors may put their short-term interests.
In most programs, a third-party provider will provide such liquidity facility; in some programs, the Firm provides this liquidity facility.
